title: First playing with Kid Rena, Lee Collins and the McCullums
summary: Just starting on his horn, Joseph played parades with Kid Rena and worked with Lee Collins and George McCullum, and they discuss the McCullums.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Oh, it was about the 20's. Right after Kelly died, he laid him out on the sand between Trayvon and Robinson in the middle on that side of the bank. He had a big few of them, Southern Stan. He did? That's right. He must have been very popular. He was. One of the best, he moved a short trumpet like that. He had a short trumpet? Yeah, he had a short one. I had one too, I got rid of it. You know the little small arm like that? I got rid of it. Did he play it too? No, he didn't play it, but he had it. And he's alright, he was a good banjo player. Gotta respect him. He come to John the days when John Morales, you remember John Morales? Yeah. Well that's the time he come up. You know. Did you play with him? I used to go with him. I was just starting out on my horn with him. Oh yeah. And I played around here with Rene, Kid Rene, on the parade. A lot of young men too. Played with Rene, around the parades. I played with Lee Collins, he's there too. Yeah. I worked with Lee Collins, at the La Vida and all. Oh yeah. And Alan Connery, that time he was upstairs with George McCubbin and all that bunch. Alvin Alcon. Oh yeah. Alvin, that's Alvin's brother I used to work with. Oh Alvin's brother, what's his name?
George McCubbin they call him, he's dead. Oh, that's Alvin's brother? Yeah, that's Alvin's brother.
Half brother. Half brother, yeah. Half brother. Now Alvin's right brother.
Well George McCullum, that was the, he was the son of the old George McCullum, wasn't he?
Yeah, that's right. The dad was a trumpet player too. That's the old man, he used to live on Louisiana Avenue, which when he lived there. I'm up there, you know.
No. Well, yeah, there's a lot of confusion there, but there's a junior and a senior.

Well, he got a son now, son and a daughter playing. I know his son is playing. I know his son, Lola, his wife they call her Lola. Nola. That's George McCullum Jr. Yeah, that's right. She had a whole lot of good records too, George. He was a good man. That man couldn't, the only way he played his horn he had to be drunk. He lost about nine horns on street cars. Oh, dear. That's right.
